chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ayub ibn Nuh from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Burd said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, we work with pig hair, so perhaps a man forgets and prays with something of it in his hand.' He said, 'It is not proper for him to pray with something of it in his hand.' And he said, 'Take it and wash it; whatever has fat/grease, do not work with it, and whatever does not have fat/grease, work with it, and wash your hands from it.'

key_terms.دَسَمٌ: Fat or grease (indicating impurity or distinct nature)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying with pig hair in hand and how to purify it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while holding pig hair during prayer does not invalidate the prayer, it is considered impure (najis) and thus not befitting for worship. The ruling distinguishes between the hair's state: if it retains its natural grease (daman), it remains impure and unsuitable for use, whereas washing away the grease renders it pure and permissible, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that removing the impurity's essence purifies the object.
